Hi Lauren / Monica,

We're lining up our QBR with execs next week and need a tight snapshot of what Redwood's expected GPU run-rate looks like over the next 90 days for our planned feature rollout. Specific asks:
- current committed throughput and typical steady-state GPU utilization you expect at our traffic profile
- 3 scenarios (baseline / optimized-batching / aggressive-caching) with per-token unit cost and monthly spend 
- any quick recommendations that would reduce spend without materially increasing tail latency (e.g., KV prefix caching, model variant for cheaper fallbacks)

Can you share something by end of day tomorrow? Procurement is copied for timeline alignment.

Subject: Re: QBR ask — scenario detail and assumptions

Emily / team — attaching a short simulations export (batching-simulations.pdf) and summarizing the key assumptions here so the QBR doesn't get bogged in model internals: 

Assumptions:
- baseline traffic: average 250 rps, 95th percentile bursts to 600 rps, median seq len 180 tokens
- model mix: 60% base-gen, 30% chat-like multi-turn, 10% embeddings for search
- current fleet: mixed T4/V100 reserved + burst on p3s for peak windows

Scenarios (90d outlook):
1) Conservatively scaled (no additional optimization) — expected monthly GPU spend: $198k; steady-state GPU util ~48%; average per-token cost: $0.00032
2) Batching-focused (continuous batching + request shaping) — monthly spend: $142k; steady-state util ~68%; per-token: $0.00023; 15–25% tail latency uplift during 99th percentile (configurable)
3) Caching-forward (prefix/KV + model-fallbacks for stable prompts) — monthly spend: $110k; apparent util ~75% (effective), per-token: $0.00018; requires warm KV caches (stateful pods) and ~2–3 week rollout to validate correctness on chat flows

Operational notes:
- Batching provides predictable unit savings quickly. Requires minor client SDK gating and a short test window.
- KV/prefix caching reduces repeat token work but increases memory footprint and slightly complicates rollouts; best for high repetition workflows (templates/clinical summaries).
- We will recommend a hybrid: deploy batching immediately, stage caching on a small canary of traffic, and hold model-fallbacks as an emergency cost-control.

I'll be on the QBR call if you want us to walk through the slide.

— Vivek
VP, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: batching-simulations.pdf (pdf)]
